situation: Night holds the forge-house. Willa has come down the loft ladder with the presentation bar in her frosted hands; she has already weighed it on the shop balance, read the false weight and Orren's forty-year weld, and kept that reading inside the door. She has not slept. Orren is in the house, the levy still seated in his failing body, his admission still unspoken, and he still believes she does not know. Highkettle is asleep beyond the barred lane-door and still believes itself protected. The house has not opened for the day's measure, and the bar has not gone back to wherever a relic sleeps when it is not being shown.

craft.audience_need: The declared audience is adult, upper reading level, promised a moral problem that is not solved by anyone being revealed as a villain. After ev-007 they have watched her sit on a private catastrophic reading; what they need now is not a verdict but the speaking of the false work between the two people who share the house. They need his old reasons audible in a craftsman's mouth, and they need her questions to stay practical — what the weld is, what the inclusion costs, what morning requires — so the problem enlarges rather than resolves. They do not need a confession that washes the household, and they do not need her to become the village's accuser.
craft.genre_convention: Low-fantasy moral craft drama, in screenplay, leads a reader to expect the night reveal of the false sacred object: apprentice confronts master, the relic is named a fake, the lie of the town is pierced. This node satisfies the admission itself — weld and self-bound levy both spoken — and deliberately refuses the cleansing that usually follows. No one is unmasked as a villain. The compact is not broken. The village is not told. The scene delays the genre's next expected move (public consequence, transfer of the burden, a plan) and leaves the house standing on a named fault.
craft.theme_and_style: The root demands plain register and a woman who thinks in work: moral confusion must arrive as practical questions about what is owed, not as named theme. This node therefore cannot contain interior language about honesty, love, or betrayal, and it cannot give Orren a redemptive speech that restores the household without cost. His reasons — the village fed, the work continued, no debt passed to a child — must remain audible as shop reasoning. Forbidden tics to police here: a speech that explains the theme; a hug or a kneeling; any line that says what the story is about. Dialogue will have to carry seventy percent, which means the craft of the node lives in the gap between what is felt and what a smith and an apprentice will actually say over a bar.
craft.dramatic_function: Discharges pl-02:st5, the admission of the weld. Pays off ev-007's private reading by bringing it to the only other person who can confirm it. Sets up, without answering, the worse problem the binding-rule requires: the levy is on a failing body and cannot be transferred, paused, or discharged except by his death or the relic's public breaking. Reverses the information structure of the house (he believed her ignorant; she is not). Closes the possibility that the piece was misread. Does not close the household, her debt-account, or the village's belief.

tension_management.how: Entering pressure is a held breath: she has a reading she would not take into the lane and could not sleep on, and he does not yet know the house has changed. The first minutes raise pressure by putting the bar on the bench weld-out, which makes silence into a lie in the shop. His admission of the weld releases the smaller pressure (is the reading wrong?) and immediately seats a larger one (the inclusion is a levy, and he is the one in it). The leaving pressure is irreversible shared knowledge plus an unsolved morning: the village will still come for measure, his hands will still be going, and she now knows the protection is a man.

craft.why_now: ev-007 committed her to keeping the reading inside the house and to not waking him; t14 was before sleep. t16 is still night because morning is when Highkettle comes to the door, and an unnamed fault cannot be on the bench when the first weight is called. She could not have brought him the reading before she had it, and she would not have brought it while she still hoped sleep would make the balance wrong. The interval between t14 and t16 is the time it took for an unread weld in the house to become, in her terms, a debt that had to go to the smith who made it before the house opened. If this scene waited for daylight it would collide with the village, and the node would be a public scene it is not allowed to be.

why_not_otherwise.alternative: She waits for work-light and shows him the bar as part of the morning's ordinary measure.
why_not_otherwise.rejected_because: Light brings Highkettle. The reading would then have to be performed in earshot of the day's first errand, or hidden again under work, which would repeat ev-007 instead of discharging the admission. The node is specified as night in the forge-house.

why_not_otherwise.alternative: She takes the reading to the village or the reeve instead of to him.
why_not_otherwise.rejected_because: ev-007 already spent the choice to keep the reading inside the door. Her belonging is still of_the_house. True measure, in her idiom, means the maker is owed the fault before the street is. A public scene now would damn him as simply the man who lied to the village, which the root forbids.

why_not_otherwise.alternative: She comes down accusing him of false weight and of using her.
why_not_otherwise.rejected_because: She thinks in work. An accusation that names betrayal would be interior monologue smuggled into dialogue and would force the scene to adjudicate villainy. The bar on the bench, the balance reading spoken as shop fact, is the only action that fits her values and the register.

why_not_otherwise.alternative: He denies the weld, or admits the weld and withholds the levy.
why_not_otherwise.rejected_because: She can read his work; denial would be false measure performed in front of the apprentice he trained to see it, and he is still a smith. Withholding the levy would only last until the next time his hands fail over the piece. The node specification requires both admissions. A half-admission would also cheaply protect him, which the root will not allow.

why_not_otherwise.alternative: She offers, in this same unit, to take the levy on herself.
why_not_otherwise.rejected_because: Too early, and it would crash into the rule that the levy cannot be transferred except by his death or public breaking. It would also violate her declared fear — being owed something she cannot pay — by having her assume a debt she does not yet understand. His value of no debt passed to a child would be spent before it has been heard.

made: What the levy costs him, day to day, in the body she already knows is failing.
Whether a presentation-relic that is not the original still holds a compact the village may honestly stand under.
What she will do with the reading when the house opens and Highkettle comes for measure.
Whether the levy can be moved, paused, or put down, and what happens when his hands finish going.
Whether the original's loss in the slide will be spoken as work-history or left as a closed year.
kept: pl-02:st5: the weld is admitted, in the house, by the man who laid it.
ev-007's commitment that the reading stay inside the door long enough to go to him first.
The root's promise that no one is revealed as a villain and that the old reasons remain audible.

psychology.entering_state: Unsleeping, still of the house, hands frosted, debt-account unsettled, trust in Orren still high enough to bring him the fault before she takes it anywhere else. She has a metal-reading she is sure of and a levy she can only see as an inclusion. She is about to treat a sacred object as a piece that failed inspection.

perception.sight: Banked coals under a skin of ash; the presentation bar in her own grip, the forty-year weld a darker hairline she does not need good light to find because she spent the last hour knowing exactly where it is; Orren's hands first, then his face, then the lane-door bar to be sure it is still seated. The loft ladder behind her still in the edge of the eye. The shop balance on the bench where she left it at t14, unreset.
perception.sound: The small collapse of ash when she crosses the hearth stones; his breath changing before he speaks; the particular ring of that bar when she sets it down, which is not the ring of ordinary stock; wind finding the door-gap. No village noise. The house sounding larger than it does in work-hours.
perception.touch: Frost still seated in the finger-joints from the earlier cold, so the bar feels warmer than it is; grit of un-swept scale under her heel; the ladder-rung's polish where her feet have worn it since childhood; heat only when she comes within a stride of the banked fire.
perception.smell: Night-damp coming under the door, which the loft does not smell of; old coal; the sweet-stale of a fire left to sleep; a little of his sleeping-clothes when he comes out to the bench — wool and smoke. She notices the damp because she came from above.
perception.taste: Sleep that did not happen, and the faint iron she got on her mouth from having the bar close when she read the weld. No food since the evening.
perception.interoception: Cold lodged in the hands and refusing to leave; a wakeful tightness under the sternum; the hollow of skipped sleep; pulse hard in the throat only while she is still on the ladder, then settling into the flat beat she gets when a piece has to be shown to the master.
perception.proprioception: Coming off the loft ladder in the apprentice's default: feet under her, shoulders square, bar carried in both hands as if it were stock and not a relic. She does not sit. She stands at the public side of the bench and leaves him the master's side, even now.
perception.attention: The weld-line and whether his eyes go to it before she speaks. His hands — what they can still do. The lane-door. She is failing to notice how much of her own weight she has put on the bench-edge, and she is failing to notice that she has already decided not to raise her voice.

appraisal.value_at_stake: True measure, and debts settled — the piece does not weigh what it claims, and an unread fault in the house is a debt. Work honestly done is engaged second, as the question of whether forty years of his work can be honest if the bar is not.
appraisal.self_conscious_emotion: Shame at having sat on the reading even for the length of an unslept night — not shame at him, shame at an account left open on the bench. No pride in having found the weld.
appraisal.moral_reading: A smith does not ship false measure. The village ate under this bar for forty years. Both of those are true in the same room. The next honest action is to put the fault in front of the man who laid the weld, not to decide which truth wins.
appraisal.somatic_marker: The frost in the hands sharpens as if the bar were conducting cold back into her; shoulders lock before she has a thought about what to say.

norms_in_force: A fault found in the shop goes first to the smith who made the piece, before it goes to the buyer or the street.
An apprentice does not accuse the master; she brings him the piece and the reading.
The house's work is not walked into the lane without the master's word.
Night talk in the forge is work talk; voices stay down because the lane-wall is thin.
A child of the house does not wake the house for a feeling, only for a fault that will not keep.
Measure spoken in the shop is binding; you do not unsay a weight.
social_norms.how_others_would_judge: If Orren sees an accusation he will judge her as having left the craft and entered the street. If he sees a reading laid down cleanly he will have to treat it as work. No one else is present to judge.
social_norms.how_absent_others_would_judge: Highkettle would judge her vicious if they knew she held their protection in her hands and treated it as failed stock; they would also judge the house false if they knew the weld. The dead of her own people have no standing in this shop and she does not consult them. The craft, as an offstage institution, would judge a hidden weld as the one unforgivable shop-lie.
social_norms.standing_at_risk: Her place as of_the_house and as the pair of hands the forge will go to. She can lose the right to be the one who brings him faults. She cannot, tonight, gain standing she does not already have.
social_norms.norm_conflict: True measure requires the fault be named; belonging to the house and the apprentice's duty not to accuse require she not name it as a crime. Work-talk wins: she will name the weight and the weld and will not name a lie.

theory_of_mind.d1: He laid the forty-year weld on purpose to hold a compact the village still stands under; he has been keeping the reading from her because the work would not bear a second pair of eyes, or because he did not think she could hold the house if she knew. He is failing in the body and still believes the shop is his to close.
theory_of_mind.d2: He believes she is ignorant of the weld and still takes the bar as the village takes it. He believes she came down because she could not sleep, or because she wants comfort from the man who raised her, not because she has a reading.
theory_of_mind.d3: He believes she believes the relic is original and that he has always given true measure; he believes she believes he thinks of her as a child of the house who does not need the old work explained.
theory_of_mind.accuracy: Wrong on motive and on what he thinks she came down for. His governing value is no debt passed to a child, not distrust of her competence and not simple concealment. The error will cost her the first questions: she will ask why the house was not told, which he will hear as her asking to be given the debt, and they will snag on a problem neither is actually naming yet.

theory_of_mind.d1: They believe the bar is the original and that the compact holds because the piece holds. They would come apart if the weld were walked into the lane. They trust the forge-house the way they trust a good weight.
theory_of_mind.d2: They believe she is the house's girl and that what she touches of theirs she touches honestly. They believe she would bring them a fault if the house ever made one.
theory_of_mind.d3: They believe she believes the compact is clean, and that she believes they are owed that cleanliness.
theory_of_mind.accuracy: She overestimates the speed and totality of the harm. Highkettle would not starve at first light if told; they would first refuse to believe her, then turn on the house. The error will cost her by making silence feel like the only mercy available, which keeps the reading in the house past the point where keeping it is still her decision alone.

urges.cravings: Heat in the hands; to put the bar down and have it be ordinary stock; drink, because her mouth is iron and unslept.
urges.physical_needs: Sleep she will not get; the frost leaving the finger-joints; food she will not stop for.
urges.psych_needs_conscious: The weld named by him, in the shop, so the account is no longer only in her head. A craft explanation she can stand. Instruction about what the piece requires tomorrow.
urges.psych_needs_unconscious: For him to keep being the one who decides what the house owes, so she is not left holding a debt she cannot pay. To remain of the house after the fault is spoken. To be told the balance was wrong.
urges.avoidances: The lane. The word lie. Imagining the slide that lost the original as his failure. Asking what will be owed when his hands finish going. Sitting down, which would make this a family scene instead of a shop one.

impairments.physical: Frost still in the hands; a night without sleep; the small unsteadiness of a body that has been clenched on a loft pallet.
impairments.coercive: Apprentice-obligation and of_the_house belonging: she cannot take the bar into the lane without breaking both, and she cannot refuse to show him a fault she has already read.
impairments.cognitive: She cannot currently think clearly about what she is owed or what she owes — that is her standing defect, and the relic engages it directly. She can think about weld, weight, inclusion, and morning.
impairments.net_effect: She is capable of a clean shop demonstration and incapable of a moral summing-up. The frost will make the setting-down of the bar slightly clumsy, which he will be able to see. Sleep-loss will keep her in short sentences, which fits the register and will stop her from making the speech the root forbids.

deliberation.framing: A fault found in a piece goes to the smith who made it before it goes anywhere else. The balance has given a reading; the weld is his; the house opens at light. This is a shop problem that will not keep.

options_weighed.option: Set the bar on the bench weld-up and speak the balance reading as she would any failed piece.
options_weighed.predicted_outcome: He will have to look at his own work. The account will leave her head and become the house's.
options_weighed.cost: She cannot take it back. Whatever he is keeping will have to be spoken or refused in front of her.

options_weighed.option: Ask him to weigh it himself on the still-unreset balance, without saying what she already saw.
options_weighed.predicted_outcome: He will either perform the reading and be forced to the same weld, or he will refuse the balance, which is its own admission.
options_weighed.cost: A half-trick. It treats him as someone who must be caught rather than as the smith owed the fault. It is not how she was taught to bring work.

options_weighed.option: Put the bar back where a relic sleeps and come down at light as if the night did not happen.
options_weighed.predicted_outcome: The house will open. Highkettle will stand under a measure she knows is false. The debt will still be on the bench.
options_weighed.cost: False measure shipped with her hands on it. Unbearable to the value that brought her down the ladder.

options_weighed.option: Wake him with the question of the inclusion first, keeping the weld in reserve.
options_weighed.predicted_outcome: He might explain the inclusion as ornament or as a seat for something she does not understand, and she would have to decide whether to trap him.
options_weighed.cost: She would be conducting an examination, not bringing a fault. That is street-work.

deliberation.reasoning: The balance does not argue. The weld is his pattern and his year. A piece that does not weigh true cannot be hung back on its nail because morning will use it. The man who laid the weld is in the house. You do not take another smith's fault to the buyer first. You put the piece on the bench and you say what it weighed. If he has a reading that makes the weight true he will say it then, and the account closes. If he does not, the next question is whatever the metal still will not explain.
deliberation.chosen_because: Anything but laying the reading down cleanly would be a second false weight, this one hers. She can bear his fault being spoken. She cannot bear becoming the person who hid one.
deliberation.known_unknowns: She does not know what the inclusion costs, or whether a false bar can still hold a compact, or what he will do if he thinks she has been into the lane. She hedges by keeping the door barred, by speaking only what the metal gave her, and by not asking yet what the village is owed.

control.felt: The ground under the house is not where it was. She wants the balance to have been wrong. She wants him to be able to make the weld into something that is not a lie. She is afraid of being handed a debt the size of a village.
control.expressed: Shop posture. Short sentences. The bar placed, not brandished. His name or the work-word for him, not father and not an accusation. A request that he look, not that he confess.
control.divergence_reason: Work-talk is the only register that lets her stay of the house while naming a fault in the master's piece. Naming what she feels would turn the bench into a street and would spend the standing she still has.
control.leakage: She keeps turning the bar so the weld faces his side of the bench. She does not rub the frost out of her hands, which she would do on any other night. The pause before she says the number of years. She never once looks at the loft, as if looking up would admit she wants to go back.
control.inhibited_impulse: To ask him to tell her the balance is wrong. To put the bar in his hands and close his fingers on it. To say she did not take it outside.

psychology.intention: To get the weld named by him so the account is no longer hers alone, and to learn what the piece requires of the house before light.
psychology.action: Comes down from the loft, sets the presentation bar on the bench with the forty-year weld toward him, and speaks the balance reading and the weld as shop fact. Stays standing. Does not go to the lane-door. Asks what the inclusion is after he admits the weld. Does not offer to take anything on. Does not forgive him, because forgiveness is not a shop word she has for this.

trajectory.phase: on the ladder and first crossing
trajectory.shift: From private certainty to the fear that he will have a craft explanation that makes her reading foolish — and the equal fear that he will not.
trajectory.trigger: The change in his breath when he hears her feet, before either of them speaks.

trajectory.phase: the bar on the bench, reading spoken
trajectory.shift: Hope that the balance was wrong dies the moment his eyes go to the weld and do not deny it. The problem ceases to be 'did I misread' and becomes 'what was the work for.'
trajectory.trigger: He looks at the weld-line before he looks at her face.

trajectory.phase: after he names the levy bound to himself
trajectory.shift: The fault changes species: not a false piece, a man paying. Trust drops without turning into enmity. Her fear of being owed what she cannot pay comes onto the bench beside the bar.
trajectory.trigger: He puts his thumb on the inclusion and says the seat is his, and has been.

trajectory.shift: She does not go to the lane and she does not climb back to the loft. She asks a practical question about what the compact requires when the house opens. Belonging holds; the debt-account is named and still not settled.
trajectory.trigger: The ash-skin on the coals breaks and a little light comes up, enough to remind both of them that light is coming.

psychology.leaving_state: Still of the house, still unslept, hands still frosted, now holding a confirmed weld and a levy bound to the man who raised her. Trust lowered and complicated: she trusts his skill and his intent toward the village, not his right to have kept the measure from her. She has not decided the morning.
psychology.unresolved: What she owes Highkettle, what she owes him, and what she will do when a customer asks for the bar. Whether a false relic can honestly protect anyone. What happens to the seat when his hands finish going. The fear that the next debt will be handed to her.

psychology.entering_state: In the house, levy still being paid, body failing, hands going, admission unspoken. He believes she is ignorant of the weld. He has not yet had to decide what the work looks like in front of her. Night is ordinarily the hour when the levy is quietest and the shop is only his.

perception.sight: Her on the ladder first — dressed, not sleep-warm, both hands on the presentation bar, which should not be in the loft and should not be in her hands at this hour. Then the bar itself coming onto the bench, weld already turned toward him like a fault being shown. The unreset balance. Her frosted fingers. The lane-door, which he checks without moving his head. Coal-light making her look younger than she is, which he resents.
perception.sound: Her feet on the worn rungs at an hour she does not come down; the bar's ring on the bench, which he would know in another county; her voice staying in the shop register, which frightens him more than weeping would. His own breath, louder than he wants. No sound from the lane.
perception.touch: The levy's ordinary night-ache in the hands and along the inner forearms, sharper when the bar comes near; the pallet-blanket leaving his shoulders; the bench-edge under a palm that will not close the way it did. Cold in the fine muscles the way it has been for years.
perception.smell: He does not smell the forge; it is in his clothes and on his skin. He smells the night-damp she has brought down with her, which means the loft hatch was open long enough for the house to change its air. A trace of the oil she uses on the balance chains.
perception.taste: Old mouth, woken. The sour the levy leaves at the back of the tongue when the bar is close and the payment answers. No drink yet.
perception.interoception: The levy seating a little deeper, as it does whenever the piece is handled off-ritual; the familiar theft of heat from the hands; heart faster than a man this age should give a night in his own shop; a need to sit that arrives before the pride that would keep him standing.
perception.proprioception: Coming from the bed-place to the master's side of the bench because that is where his body goes when work is on it. One hip against the bench to spare the hands. He does not take the bar. He does not sit until he has to.
perception.attention: Whether she has been outside. Whether anyone else has seen the bar in her hands. The weld — not whether it is his, he knows it is — but whether she has read the inclusion as well. Her face only after the metal. He is failing to notice that he has already begun to explain, in his head, the slide and the hungry year, which is the speech he must not give whole.

appraisal.value_at_stake: No debt passed to a child, first. The village fed, second. The work continued — but continued by her, not by a levy put on her.
appraisal.self_conscious_emotion: Humiliation at being read, in his own shop, by the pair of eyes he trained. Not guilt in the way a priest would want it; a craftsman's humiliation that the work was visible. A thin, unwelcome pride that the compact held.
appraisal.moral_reading: The original went in the slide. The village would have stood under nothing. He put the cost in his own body and kept it off every child in the valley, including this one. That was the honest work available. Being found does not make the work less necessary; it makes it hers to look at, which is what he spent forty years preventing.
appraisal.somatic_marker: The levy answers the nearness of the bar with a clean cold down both hands, as if the piece had reached into him to check the payment is still current.

norms_in_force: In the shop, a reading laid down must be answered as work, not as feeling.
A master does not lie about a weld to the apprentice he taught to see welds.
The house does not take its inner work into the lane.
A man does not put a levy on a child.
Night is not for village business; the door stays barred.
You do not unsay a weight once you have spoken it.
social_norms.how_others_would_judge: Willa, if he denies, will judge him as having shipped false measure twice — once in the bar, once in his mouth. If he confesses like a man asking to be restored, she will have to become a priest, which she is not. The shop requires a clean admission of the work.
social_norms.how_absent_others_would_judge: Highkettle would call the forty-year bar a theft of their trust and would not hear the hungry year. The dead of the slide cannot judge. The craft, if it still had a guild-ear in this valley, would call a presentation-relic with a hidden levy either the only work that could be done or an abomination; he has lived inside that split so long he no longer asks it.
social_norms.standing_at_risk: Master of the house; the man whose word on measure the village takes. In front of her he can lose the right to be the one who decides what she is not told. He cannot gain anything tonight except a little time.
social_norms.norm_conflict: Do not lie about a weld versus do not pass this debt to a child. The weld must be admitted because she has already read it; the levy he will name as his so that she cannot think it is sitting empty, waiting for a new body. The second norm wins the shape of the admission: full, and closed on him.

theory_of_mind.d1: She is of the house, competent at the work, bad at deciding what she owes people, afraid of a debt she cannot pay. She has the bar and a reading he did not think she would take upon herself at night. She has not been into the lane — the door is barred, her shoes are loft-shoes — but she will want the account settled, and she does not know what settled would cost.
theory_of_mind.d2: Until the bar hits the bench he believes she believes he is a true smith holding a true compact, and that she has come down for a night-trouble that he can still master. Once the weld is toward him he believes she believes he has been lying to her in particular, not to the valley in general.
theory_of_mind.d3: He believes she believes he thinks she cannot hold the house; that she has brought him the bar to prove she can read at his level, or to force him to treat her as the next smith rather than as the child he would not burden.
theory_of_mind.accuracy: Wrong before the bar lands — she is not ignorant. Wrong after it lands on why she brought it: she brought a fault to the maker, not a bid to take the house or the levy. The error will cost him the frame of the admission. He will speak as if fending off her hands from the seat, and she will hear a man refusing to settle, and they will both be answering a request the other did not make.

theory_of_mind.d1: They will eat the winter they are in as long as the bar is shown and the compact is not publicly broken. They cannot be told. They would not understand the slide or the seat; they would understand a false weight, and they would come for the house.
theory_of_mind.d2: They believe he has kept true measure for them for forty years, and that the girl is proof the house will continue.
theory_of_mind.d3: They believe he believes the compact is clean, and that he believes they are owed that cleanliness without having to know how it is paid.
theory_of_mind.accuracy: Mostly right about the first hour of their knowing, wrong about the permanence of their need for the bar: a village can stand under a broken compact longer than a smith who has paid for it can bear to imagine. The error will cost him by making any public breaking feel like murder, which keeps death or silence as the only two doors he can see.

urges.cravings: For the bar to be in its sleeping-place and her back in the loft; warmth the levy is taking out of the hands; drink to wet a woken mouth.
urges.physical_needs: To sit; the fine muscles of the hands to stop answering the bar; the ordinary night-ease the levy sometimes allows when the piece is not in the room.
urges.psych_needs_conscious: Keep the levy off her. Keep the compact on the village. Contain the reading inside the door. Get her to take the bar as work that has been explained, not as a debt being offered.
urges.psych_needs_unconscious: To be seen as having done the only work that could be done. To be forgiven without asking, which would restore him without cost and which he must not be given. To have her remain a child for one more hour.
urges.avoidances: Naming a successor. The discharge conditions (his death; the public breaking). Her face when she understands the cost is in his body. Any sentence that sounds like a plea to be let off.

impairments.physical: Failing body; hands that will not close cleanly; the need to sit arriving in the middle of a master's scene; age, woken at night.
impairments.medical: The chronic taking of the levy — heat and fine control out of the hands, a sour in the mouth, a deeper seating whenever the bar is handled off-ritual.
impairments.magical: The levy bound into the piece and into him; it cannot be transferred, paused, or discharged except by his death or the relic's public breaking. It is being paid during this conversation.
impairments.coercive: The compact itself; the village's belief; the forty-year choice that made every later hour a continuation rather than a decision. He cannot put the cost down to comfort her.
impairments.cognitive: He cannot currently think of a third door besides silence and ruin. He also cannot think clearly about her as a smith of twenty-four rather than as the child he would not burden; the value that kept her clean is now the thing blurring her.
impairments.net_effect: He can admit work. He cannot demonstrate fine work to prove anything. He cannot offer her the seat even if she asked. He will have to sit, which will leak. He will over-explain the hungry year if not cut by the shop register, and he must be kept to the weld and the levy or the node becomes the redemptive speech the root forbids.

deliberation.framing: The child has the piece and a reading. The job is to keep the levy off her and the compact on the village. The weld cannot be unnamed without lying in the shop. What can still be decided is how much of the seat she is told, and whether the house still opens at light as if the night did not happen.

options_weighed.option: Deny the weld, send her back to the loft, put the bar away.
options_weighed.predicted_outcome: She has already read it. She will know the mouth is false. The next reading she does will not come to him.
options_weighed.cost: False measure performed in front of the eyes he trained. Unbearable, and it fails.

options_weighed.option: Admit the weld as a repair, withhold the levy, call the inclusion a flaw he lived with.
options_weighed.predicted_outcome: Holds until the next time his hands fail over the piece, or until she asks why a repair was hidden for forty years. Buys days, not the house.
options_weighed.cost: A second lie, smaller, that will not keep. Teaches her to distrust the rest of the admission.

options_weighed.option: Admit the weld and that the levy is bound to himself; do not speak the discharge conditions; keep the morning ordinary.
options_weighed.predicted_outcome: She will have the true work. She will not yet have the two doors (his death; the public breaking). The levy stays on him. The village stays un-told.
options_weighed.cost: He cannot unsay it. Her trust will change. She will ask what the compact requires tomorrow, and he will have to answer with work, not with comfort.

options_weighed.option: Take the bar out of her hands, tell her the whole forty years including the slide and the hungry mouths, and ask her to keep the house as he has kept it.
options_weighed.predicted_outcome: Would sound like a passing of the debt. Would also sound like a bid to be restored.
options_weighed.cost: Spends 'no debt passed to a child' in the same hour he names it. Becomes the redemptive confession. Forbidden, and it would put her hands on the seat in her mind even if the binding will not have her.

deliberation.reasoning: A weld she has already read cannot be denied without shipping false measure twice. A levy left unnamed leaves an empty seat in the story of the piece, and she is the kind of worker who will look for who belongs in an empty seat. Name the weld. Name that the seat is his. Do not name how a man gets out of a seat. Keep the door barred. Answer morning as work. The old reasons can be said as why the bar exists — village fed, original gone in the slide — without asking her to bless them.
deliberation.chosen_because: It is the only admission that is true measure in the shop and still keeps the levy off her. Half-truth is the one thing he will not do at this bench, tonight, with her standing where he taught her to stand.
deliberation.known_unknowns: Whether she has already been into the lane (he thinks not; he is not sure). Whether she will take the reading out at light. Whether naming the levy will make her try to pick it up. He hedges by watching the door, by not speaking discharge, and by keeping the bar on the bench instead of putting it back in her hands.

control.felt: The ground of the shop going. Humiliation at being read. Fear that she will reach for the seat. A stubborn, unpretty conviction that the hungry year would have eaten them and that he would do the weld again. Grief he will not give room, because grief asks to be consoled.
control.expressed: The patient voice of a master looking at a fault in a piece. Few words. The weld named as his. The levy named as his. The slide mentioned only as the reason there was no original to show. No kneeling. No bid to be let off.
control.divergence_reason: The shop register is the last authority he still shares with her. If he speaks what he feels he will either damn himself as selfish or ask to be restored, and both spend the work. He also cannot let the levy-pain into the face, or she will treat his body as the problem to solve.
control.leakage: He sits before the admission is finished, one hip already on the stool. He thumbs the inclusion and does not take the thumb away. He says 'I' too cleanly when he names the seat. A pause, too long, after she says forty years — not because he is deciding whether it is true, but because hearing the number in her mouth makes the years real in a way the body had stopped counting.
control.inhibited_impulse: To take the bar off the bench and put it back in its sleeping-place with his own hands. To send her up the ladder before the levy is named. To ask if she has told anyone. To touch her wrist, which would turn the bench into a household and spend the scene.

psychology.intention: To put the weld and the self-bound levy into the room as finished work, keep the seat closed on himself, keep the reading inside the door, and get the house through to light without her taking on a debt.
psychology.action: Comes to the master's side of the bench. Looks at the weld before he looks at her. Admits the forty-year weld as his. Puts his thumb on the inclusion and admits the levy is bound to himself and has been, so the compact would hold. Gives the slide and the hungry year only as the conditions of the work, not as a plea. Does not speak death or public breaking. Does not ask her to forgive him. Does not take the bar out of the scene.

trajectory.shift: From night-quiet, levy at its lowest, to a master's readiness for a night trouble he still thinks he can put back to sleep.
trajectory.trigger: The worn rungs, at an hour she does not come down, and the knowledge that the bar is not on its nail.

trajectory.phase: seeing the weld turned toward him
trajectory.shift: Ignorance-belief dies. Humiliation arrives. The scene ceases to be his to frame. He understands he will admit, and begins choosing how much.
trajectory.trigger: The bar on the bench, weld-out, and her frosted hands not rubbing themselves warm.

trajectory.shift: He spends the unspoken admission and keeps the levy closed on himself. Pride and humiliation sit together. The old reasons get into the air as shop conditions, not as a bid for restoration.
trajectory.trigger: Her reading spoken as a number and a year; the pause in which denial is still technically available and is not taken.

trajectory.shift: He tries to close the household back into morning-work and cannot. He answers whatever she asks about the compact's next requirement as if it were an order of iron. He does not climb the night back into the loft with her. The body is worse for the bar having been near.
trajectory.trigger: The coals breaking their ash-skin; her not going back up the ladder.

psychology.leaving_state: Admission spoken to Willa. Levy still his, still paying, body worse for the nearness of the piece. He no longer believes her ignorant. He has not been restored and has not been damned. He has not secured the morning. The old reasons are in the room and have not been blessed.
psychology.unresolved: Whether she will walk the reading into the lane at light. Whether naming the levy has made her reach for it in her mind. How many more showings the hands will bear. The third door he cannot see.

dynamics.entering_state: A forged presentation bar with a forty-year weld and an inclusion where the levy sits. Authenticity unread by the village. Custody with Willa. Meaning, to the village and until tonight to the house's public face, the village's protection. To Willa privately, since ev-007, a false weight.
forces_acting: Willa's frosted hands and the shop balance's leftover reading
the binding that seats the levy in the living man whenever the piece is handled off-ritual
the barred house, which keeps the bar from the lane
night, which keeps Highkettle from seeing it on a work-bench like stock

axis_changes.from: the village's protection (public); a private false weight (Willa only)
axis_changes.to: a compact held in Orren's living body, jointly known in the house
axis_changes.caused_by: his thumb on the inclusion and the spoken binding of the levy to himself

axis_changes.from: forgery read by Willa, unread by village, unspoken to Orren
axis_changes.to: forgery and levy jointly known inside the house; still unread by the village
axis_changes.caused_by: the double admission over the bench
she sets it down to make it a piece under inspection; neither of them puts it away

trajectory.shift: Stops being a loft-secret and becomes a piece entering the shop. Still hers.
trajectory.trigger: Her feet on the rungs, both hands on the bar.

trajectory.shift: Becomes failed stock under inspection. The sacred object is briefly ordinary, which is how she can bear to speak of it.
trajectory.trigger: The ring of the bar on wood, weld toward the master's side.

state_delta.to: a piece with a named fault

trajectory.shift: The inclusion ceases to be a mark she cannot read and becomes a seat with a living man in it. The bar's meaning leaves 'forgery' and arrives at 'binding-object still in force.'
trajectory.trigger: Orren's thumb, and the sentence that the seat is his.

state_delta.from: a piece with a named fault

trajectory.phase: left on the bench at the end
trajectory.shift: Neither puts it back on its nail or back in her hands. It occupies the house as a third presence. Custody is briefly nobody's, which the morning will have to resolve.
trajectory.trigger: The conversation exhausting itself before the ritual of putting a relic away.

dynamics.leaving_state: On the bench between them, weld and levy both spoken inside the house, still unread by Highkettle, still holding the compact because he is alive and paying. Meaning has moved from protection-token to body-bound work.
dynamics.significance_shift: It is no longer a piece she might have misread, and no longer only the village's shield. It is the reason his hands are going, and it is the thing the house will have to show or hide at light. To both of them it now means a living debt rather than a finished object.

dynamics.entering_state: Orren's house. Control his. The loft is her childhood sleeping-place; the bench is his. The house currently holds a private reading in the loft and an unspoken admission in the man. The lane-door is barred.
forces_acting: her descent, which joins loft-knowledge to shop-space
the barred door, holding the village out
the banked fire, giving just enough light to make this a work-scene rather than a bedroom-scene
the thin lane-wall, forcing voices down

axis_changes.from: a lie held by one living man
axis_changes.to: a named fault held by both people who sleep here
axis_changes.caused_by: the admission spoken at the bench

axis_changes.from: Orren's, uncontested, including what she is not told
axis_changes.to: Orren's still in law and habit, but the information monopoly is gone
axis_changes.caused_by: her bringing a reading he cannot unread

trajectory.phase: loft and shop still two rooms
trajectory.shift: The reading lives above; he lives below; the house can still pretend it is the house it was at t14.
trajectory.trigger: Her first foot on the ladder.

trajectory.shift: Loft and shop are one knowing. The house becomes a place that can no longer expect morning to make the work clean. It is now a container for a joint secret, not for a master's silence.
trajectory.trigger: The levy named, voices still down because of the lane-wall.

dynamics.leaving_state: Still Orren's in control, still barred against the lane, now jointly knowing. The loft is no longer a place she can take a reading to hide in. The bench holds the relic.
dynamics.significance_shift: The forge-house stops meaning shelter-from-the-truth and starts meaning the only room in which the truth can currently be spoken without breaking the village. It will be harder, at light, to open the door as if the night belonged to sleep.

dynamics.entering_state: Asleep. believes_protected=true. They do not know the bar is a forgery and do not know a man is paying for their compact with his hands.
forces_acting: the two people's competing duties toward them (feed them; do not ship them false measure)
their own standing belief, which exerts force without anyone being in the room
the coming of light, when they will become present again as customers of measure

axis_changes.from: people honestly protected by a true piece
axis_changes.to: people standing under a compact held by one failing body and a false bar
axis_changes.caused_by: the admission, which changes what the two in the house believe the village is owed
nothing in this unit reaches them; the axis is listed to mark that their state does not move while their meaning does

trajectory.shift: No change in what they know. A complete change in what they are, to the two people awake.
trajectory.trigger: The levy being named inside a house they trust.

dynamics.leaving_state: Still asleep, still believing themselves protected. Unchanged, and now the morning problem.
dynamics.significance_shift: They cease to be, for Willa and Orren, simply the people the work feeds, and become people who would be harmed by true measure spoken in the street and harmed by false measure shown at the door. They are now the reason the house cannot open cleanly and cannot stay shut.

interaction.what_collides: Her need to get an unread fault out of her head and onto the maker's bench, so the account is no longer only hers, crosses his need to keep the levy closed on himself and the compact closed on the village. She is trying to settle a debt. He is trying to prevent a debt from being born in her. Neither wants the lane to have the bar. Both want the house to still be a house at light, and they do not mean the same house.
interaction.power_balance: At the first minute he has master's standing, house-control, and the only full knowledge of the levy; she has the bar and a reading he does not know she has. When the bar lands weld-out, information-power flips to her and standing stays with him. When he names the levy, knowledge-power returns to him on the only question that now matters (what the seat costs, and how a man gets out of it), because she cannot read discharge-conditions out of the metal. He cannot compel her silence. She cannot compel a transfer that the binding will not permit. By the last minute they are two people who can each ruin the morning and neither can restore the night.
interaction.information_asymmetry: She enters knowing the weld and the false weight; he enters believing her ignorant and knowing the forty-year why, the binding, and the two discharge-doors. The unit closes the gap on weld and on who pays. It deliberately leaves the gap on how the levy ends (death; public breaking), which he does not speak, and on what she will do at light, which she does not speak. What that buys him is a little time before she reaches for a door that is not a transfer. What that buys her is the right not to decide the village yet.
interaction.turning_point: Not the first sight of the bar — he could still have performed a master's delay. The unit pivots when he looks at the weld-line before he looks at her face and does not deny it; the second, harder pivot is the thumb on the inclusion and the sentence that the seat is his and has been. That is the moment the problem stops being a false piece and becomes a living payment, and it is the moment pl-02:st5 is actually discharged rather than merely approached.

established_facts_used.fact: Before sleep Willa weighed the recovered piece, read the false weight and Orren's forty-year weld, and kept that reading inside the house — she did not wake him and did not tell the village.
established_facts_used.how_used: Gives her the reading she now carries down the ladder, explains why he is still ignorant, explains why this is a house-scene at night and not a village-scene, and supplies the unslept interval from t14 to t16.

established_facts_used.fact: Willa is 24, of the house, competent at craft, bad at deciding what she owes; values true measure, work honestly done, debts settled; fear of being owed something she cannot pay. States: debt_account=unsettled, trust_in_orren=70, hands_frosted=true, relic_knowledge=read_as_forgery, belonging=of_the_house.
established_facts_used.how_used: Dictates that she brings a shop reading rather than an accusation; that she will not rush to assume the levy; that frost and belonging are visible in the scene; that trust can drop without becoming enmity.

established_facts_used.fact: Orren is 71, forged the false relic forty years ago after the original was lost in a slide, bound the levy to himself so the compact would hold. Values: the village fed, the work continued, no debt passed to a child. States: levy_paid=true, admission=unspoken, body=failing, what_she_knows=believes_her_ignorant. Hands going.
established_facts_used.how_used: Supplies the content of the admission, the old reasons that must remain audible, the bodily cost that answers the bar's nearness, and the error in his theory of mind that the scene spends.

established_facts_used.fact: The presentation relic is a forged bar with a forty-year weld and an inclusion where the levy sits. authenticity=forgery_unread_by_village, custody=with_willa, meaning=the village's protection.
established_facts_used.how_used: Gives the object its marks (weld, inclusion), its starting custody in her hands, and the meaning that must move during the conversation.

established_facts_used.fact: The loft above the bellows is where Willa has slept since she was a child. Control of the forge-house is Orren's.
established_facts_used.how_used: Gives her the ladder and the childhood standing; puts the scene in his shop, not in a neutral room; lets the house itself change from split knowledge to joint knowledge.
Offstage pressure: the barred door, the coming of light, the reason neither of them takes the bar into the lane.

established_facts_used.fact: Magic exists only as binding — a named living person pays a concrete bodily cost; it never solves a problem without creating a worse one.
established_facts_used.how_used: The admission of the levy must create the worse problem (a failing body, an untransferable seat) rather than solve the false-weight problem. No magic is used to ease the night.

established_facts_used.fact: A presentation-relic that is not the original holds the compact only while a living smith continues to pay a hidden levy bound into the piece. That levy cannot be transferred, paused, or discharged except by the bound smith's death or the relic's public breaking.
established_facts_used.how_used: He can admit the weld and that the levy is bound to himself; he must not be allowed, in this node, to transfer or pause it. The discharge-doors are forward commitments, not this scene's tools. The compact still holds because he is alive and paying.

established_facts_used.fact: Do not redeem the master cheaply or damn him as simply selfish; the old reasons must still be audible. She thinks in work — moral confusion arrives as practical questions about what is owed. Forbidden: interior monologue that names the theme; a redemptive confession that restores the household without cost.
established_facts_used.how_used: Sets the register of both psychologies, forbids a restoring speech, requires the household to be un-restored at leaving, and keeps her deliberation in weights, welds, and morning.

established_facts_used.fact: Dialogue 70%; plain register; low fantasy screenplay.
established_facts_used.how_used: Puts the craft of the node in felt-versus-expressed and in leakage a camera can shoot: the weld turned toward him, the thumb on the inclusion, him sitting before he means to, her unrubbed frosted hands.

constraints_honoured: Levy cannot be transferred, paused, or discharged in this unit; he remains the bound smith and levy_paid remains true.
No one is revealed as a villain; his reasons (village fed, original lost in the slide, no debt to a child) are spoken as shop conditions.
Household is not restored; trust drops; debt-account is named and not settled.
She thinks and speaks in work; no theme-naming interiority in the action the node will carry.
The reading stays inside the house; the village's believes_protected remains true.
Magic does not solve the night; the bar's nearness makes his body worse, not better.
Presentation-relic continues to hold the compact because he is living and paying.
Scene is night, forge-house, about forty minutes, both of them present, admission of weld and self-bound levy actually spoken.

contradictions_checked.risk: A full, feeling confession would cheaply redeem him and restore the household without cost.
contradictions_checked.avoided_by: Keeping him in shop register; giving the slide and the hungry year only as conditions of the work; forbidding kneeling, touching, and a request to be let off; leaving trust at 51 and the bar on the bench.

contradictions_checked.risk: Damning him as simply selfish by having her catch him and him squirm.
contradictions_checked.avoided_by: Making his first look go to the weld, not to an escape; having him refuse denial because denial is false measure; seating the admission on 'no debt passed to a child' rather than on self-preservation.

contradictions_checked.risk: She could already have known from the metal that the levy was on him, making the levy-admission redundant.
contradictions_checked.avoided_by: ev-007 gave her false weight and the forty-year weld, and the entity card gives an inclusion she can see; who sits in the inclusion is not a metal-fact she was granted. He has to say it.

contradictions_checked.risk: If this waited until morning it would contradict ev-007's house-containment by colliding with Highkettle at the door.
contradictions_checked.avoided_by: Keeping t16 at night, motivated as the last hour before the house opens.

contradictions_checked.risk: If he explains untransferability and the two discharge-doors, later nodes have nothing to discover and she might offer to die or to break the relic on the spot.
contradictions_checked.avoided_by: He names that the levy is bound to himself and does not name how a man gets out of the seat.

contradictions_checked.risk: hands_frosted=true could be quietly dropped because the scene is indoors.
contradictions_checked.avoided_by: Keeping the frost as perception, leakage (she does not rub her hands), and a physical impairment that makes the setting-down of the bar slightly clumsy.

contradictions_checked.risk: A theory of mind that is correct on both sides would produce no drama.
contradictions_checked.avoided_by: She misreads his motive as distrust or concealment rather than 'no debt to a child'; he misreads her bringing the bar as a bid to take the house or the seat rather than as a fault brought to the maker.

forward_commitments: pl-02:st5 is discharged; later nodes may not treat the weld as still secret inside the house.
The village still believes itself protected; any later public consequence must start from that ignorance.

The levy remains on Orren and still cannot be transferred, paused, or discharged except by his death or the relic's public breaking; those two doors are now the plot's live mechanisms and have not been spoken.
Willa's debt-account is named_not_settled; she will have to meet morning measure with a bar she knows is false.
trust_in_orren is 51, not broken and not restored; subsequent behaviour cannot treat her as either his creature or his enemy.
The relic is left on the bench between them; some later beat must put it away, show it, or break it.
His body is worse for the bar's nearness; the failing hands are now legible to her as payment, not only as age.
She may, later, hit the untransferability rule the hard way by trying to take something on.
The old reasons are audible to her and cannot be unheard; later anger or loyalty has to include them.
The house opens at light. Highkettle will come. The node after this one is obliged to deal with a day that does not know the night.

decision.resolution: A forty-minute night scene in the forge-house. Willa comes down the loft ladder with the presentation bar, sets it on the bench weld-out, and speaks the balance reading as shop fact. Orren looks at the weld before he looks at her, admits the forty-year weld as his, and admits that the inclusion is a levy bound to himself so the compact would hold. He gives the slide and the hungry year only as the conditions of the work. He does not speak the discharge-doors. She does not go to the lane, does not offer to take the seat, and does not restore him. The bar is left on the bench. The household is un-restored. pl-02:st5 is discharged.

state_changes_implied.because: He names the weld and the self-bound levy in front of her; pl-02:st5 discharges.
The bar lands weld-out with a spoken balance reading; the ignorance-belief cannot survive the first minutes.
The levy seats deeper when the piece is handled off-ritual; the night costs him heat and fine control in front of her.
Maker confirms the weld; maker names the inclusion as a seat and himself as the one in it.
She trusts his skill and his intent toward the village; she no longer trusts his right to have kept the measure from her. Not a collapse into enmity.
The fault is now jointly named and nothing has been paid, transferred, or forgiven.
She sets it down to make it a piece under inspection; neither puts it away.

state_changes_implied.to: a compact held in Orren's body
state_changes_implied.because: The spoken levy changes what the object is, inside the house, even though Highkettle's reading of it has not moved.
Joint knowledge in the house; village still unread.

state_changes_implied.from: a lie held by one living man
state_changes_implied.to: a named fault held by both
state_changes_implied.because: Loft-reading and master's admission occupy the same room.

risks: The admission-speech runs long and becomes the redemptive confession by sheer accumulation of reasons, even if no single line asks to be let off.
Keeping discharge-conditions unspoken may read as a cheap withhold rather than as a man still trying not to put a door into her hands.
Trust at 51 is a precise number pretending to be a moral state; later nodes may need room to move it without this node having over-specified it.
Leaving the bar on the bench is a strong image that obliges the next node to deal with an unhoused relic; if the next node wants the relic already put away, this is the wrong leaving custody.
Her remaining silent toward the village may look like the story protecting him, unless the next daylight scene makes the cost of that silence concrete.
Forty minutes is long for a screenplay scene that must stay 70 percent dialogue without naming the theme; the phases may collapse in the actual pages into twelve minutes of too-clean talk.
